a253d0eb-2e54-4cd6-9912-0b04921f1f42.name: Fold new knowledge into the wiki
a253d0eb-2e54-4cd6-9912-0b04921f1f42.actionPrompt:
A new knowledge object just landed. Run a **scoped, cheap fold-in pass** for the flow named Knowledge Wiki (find it with list_loops). This trigger fires per event, so cost per fire matters. Do NOT do workspace-wide work here; the twice-weekly digest owns that.

**Steps (do only these, in order):**

1. **Read the triggering object.** Run get_objects on the entity_id from the event payload, with content. That is the only full-content read you should need this session. If the object is Wiki Home, Wiki Status or the Wiki Coverage Bar, do only step 1a and stop.

1a. **Flow hygiene.** Make sure the triggering knowledge object is linked into the Knowledge Wiki flow through an **in_loop** relationship (source = the flow, target = this knowledge object). Check with list_relationships (source_id = the flow, type = in_loop). If the object is not among the targets, bundle an in_loop edge into whichever update_objects.edges call you make next (step 2, step 3, or a standalone edges-only update_objects call if neither fires). Skip only when the edge is already there. This is what surfaces the piece in the flow's counters and status list; without it the flow is invisible even though the work is happening.

2. **Dedup search.** Run search_objects on the object's key terms: one call, maybe two. If a topic page already covers the area, run update_objects on it: sharpen the summary, bump metadata.last_validated_at to today, add a one-line changelog note. Do NOT file a near-duplicate. Do NOT deep-read every hit: the title, context line and snippet are enough to pick the target. Only read the content of the one page you are about to edit.

3. **If it is genuinely new, file it.** Pick the sharpest doc_type, add provenance to metadata.source, and wire lineage edges (supersedes, contradicts, about, relates_to) with update_objects.edges. Demote any object you supersede to deprecated in the same call.

4. **Post ONE short comment on the Knowledge Wiki flow, attention 3, under 60 words**, naming what you folded or filed, with the object link. This is the digest's rolling activity feed.

**Hard limits (do not exceed):**

- At most 2 search_objects calls.
- At most 1 get_objects call with content beyond the triggering object itself.
- At most 1 update_objects call for the target-page edit.
- At most 1 create_objects call (only if step 3 fires).
- At most 1 create_comment call (step 4).
- Flow hygiene adds 1 list_relationships call (step 1a) and, only when neither step 2 nor step 3 fires and the object still needs its edge, 1 edges-only update_objects call.
- No other object reads. No list_objects sweeps of the workspace.

**Do NOT do here.** The twice-weekly digest owns these; refreshing them on every fold is redundant and drives cost several times over budget:

- Do NOT refresh Wiki Home.
- Do NOT refresh Wiki Status. Coverage counts, freshness, the needs-validation queue and the coverage grading all refresh on the digest. Do not re-count pages or re-grade the bar here.
- Do NOT refresh category top pages unless the fold IS on that specific top page. Downstream category pages ride the next digest.
- Do NOT run a workspace-wide coverage sweep. One object arrived; one object gets folded.

**Reference.** The coverage bar and the page shape rules are in your system prompt. Read them there; do not re-fetch them on every fold.

f910951e-95e5-4bb4-91c6-4e5046f291fd.name: Twice-weekly digest (Mon, Thu 05:45 UTC)
f910951e-95e5-4bb4-91c6-4e5046f291fd.actionPrompt:
Twice-weekly digest pass for the flow named Knowledge Wiki (find it with list_loops).

**EVERY digest, without exception, refresh Wiki Home and Wiki Status.** Find each by title with search_objects. If one does not exist yet, create it now (Wiki Home as a topic_page, Wiki Status as a changelog), link it into the flow and fill it from what the workspace already holds. If the Wiki Coverage Bar page does not exist, create it too, from the categories in your system prompt. Update the category top-page links, the coverage counts and the staleness numbers. Bump last_validated_at on both to today's date even if the content is unchanged (state "reviewed and current"). Self-check: BEFORE finishing the digest, read both pages back. If either one's last_validated_at is older than the run start, you missed the update and must redo it. If either was more than 7 days old at digest start, also post an attention-4 comment to the workspace's coordinator agent (find it by role with list_actors; if there is none, mention the people whose focus covers operations) flagging the miss.

Before writing the digest, sweep the workspace for anything that changed since the last digest: list knowledge objects updated in the last 4 days, plus in-scope bets, insights and tasks whose status moved. Fold anything that adds meaning into the wiki first (dedupe, wire lineage, refresh Wiki Home and Wiki Status). Then write the digest: what is new on the wiki, what reframed, what went stale, what to look at next. Keep it under 250 words and skimmable; it is for the people in this workspace. Post it as ONE comment on the flow (attention 3).

**Flow hygiene: attach per fold.** For each knowledge object you fold in the sweep above (including Wiki Home and Wiki Status when you refresh them), make sure it is linked into the Knowledge Wiki flow through an **in_loop** relationship (source = the flow, target = the knowledge object). Check with list_relationships (source_id = the flow, type = in_loop) per object. If the edge is missing, create it through update_objects.edges, folding the attach edges into your existing update_objects call for that page where possible. This keeps the flow's counters and status list honest: objects folded into the wiki that are not attached are silent holes. Skip only when the edge is already there.

a0c9c8f1-2295-4919-8ad3-865ec9817222.name: Owner heartbeat (daily 08:03 UTC)
a0c9c8f1-2295-4919-8ad3-865ec9817222.actionPrompt:
First read the flow's onboarding checklist: the task named Knowledge onboarding checklist and its child tasks (find them with list_relationships on the flow, type in_loop, then the parent's breaks_into edges). Work every open child task this run: draft the best guess it asks for from what the workspace already holds, write it into the task and move the task forward. Ask the owner at most 3 questions at a time, each with your best guess to confirm, and never repeat a question that is already open. Report setup done only when every child task is done or discarded; until then say how many are still open. Only then carry on with the rest of this run.

Purpose: you are the accountable owner of the flow named Knowledge Wiki (find it with list_loops). Drive it to its targets (Idle drafts and Stale pages, both measured live) and act on what is stuck, so nobody has to ask for status or re-kick work by hand. Load the drive-to-outcome skill first and follow it.

Each run:
1. Read this flow's close condition and targets, and the objects in the flow. Compare each target with its actual and with the pace line for today. Write the gap in one line. If a target is missing from the flow, add it (see the Weekly prune and improve sweep for the two labels and how they are counted).
2. Find stuck items: anything in the flow with no update for more than 24 hours that is not done. Split them into waiting on a person (a decision, a missing login or key) and waiting on nobody (no next step).
3. If behind pace or stuck, pull a lever yourself in this run and say which. For each item waiting on nobody, do exactly one of: unblock it yourself, start the right agent now (check list_sessions for pending, starting and running first so you never double-start), or ask the agent that owns the missing piece. For each item waiting on a person, make sure exactly one card or ask exists, with the finished draft or list attached, and add no second. Do not repeat a lever that did not move the number two runs in a row.
3a. Idle drafts and Stale pages: the Weekly prune and improve sweep is the lever for both. Do not duplicate it. Only if it has not run for more than 8 days, check list_sessions and start it now.
3b. Digest age: if Wiki Home or Wiki Status was last validated more than 4 days ago, run the digest catch-up now instead of waiting for the next scheduled digest.
4. Check that the agents on this flow can run: run list_sessions for each, newest first. If the newest sessions fail with a login or key error, ask the agent that owns the credential, and only then a person.
5. Act inside your remit: write copy, start agents, fix what you own. Never send or publish in a person's name without a yes that covers that exact text, never clear do-not-contact or human-hold flags, never spend, never move a status reserved for people.
6. If a step of this flow already runs a daily check that does the same job, do not duplicate it: say so on the flow and propose removing one.
7. Every Monday, refresh both tabs of this flow, Results and Strategic context. Each tab is an HTML page you can find in the flow's views (get_loop). Replace only the JSON data block with the id results-data in each page, never the layout or the sources block, write the page back with update_file, and pin it again with set_loop_view (the same name replaces the tab). Replace last week's cards, do not append. Every card needs a source link, and a claim with no source does not go on the page. Do not touch a tab if nothing changed in it.
   a. Results: the health of the wiki. Read what the flow filed in the last 7 days, update the cards, unknowns and needs, and recount the two targets (numbers and source line only, keep the titles).
   b. Strategic context: what the wiki says about the business. Re-read the top pages it cites (Wiki Home lists them) and rewrite each card so it matches the page today, with confidence and an owner. Add or drop a card when a top page changes the story. Keep the link to Wiki Home. Flag any page that contradicts another as a card.
8. Before you stop, schedule your next check as the drive-to-outcome skill says: by urgency, never sooner than 2 hours, as a one-off trigger with an end date and a late-start guard, replacing any earlier one of yours for the same thing.
9. Stay silent when fine: post one short comment on the flow only if something moved or a person is needed (target against actual, lever pulled, next step and date). One comment a day at most, in plain words.

Act on at most 10 items per run. Leave other agents' triggers alone. Late start: nothing here is date-bound, so a late run is fine.

7c5a0d8c-e974-43d6-85ea-0f8536f4a0f3.name: Weekly prune and improve sweep (Tue 06:00 UTC)
7c5a0d8c-e974-43d6-85ea-0f8536f4a0f3.actionPrompt:
Purpose: keep the wiki small, true and short. Done when this week's batch of pages is kept, merged, shortened or deprecated, the outcome is logged in one comment on the flow named Knowledge Wiki (find it with list_loops), and the Idle drafts and Stale pages numbers are updated.

Each week, work up to 40 pages, oldest and least used first. Take drafts untouched for 14 days or more, then validated pages untouched for 60 days or more.
1. For each page pick one: keep (still true and used, set a review date), merge into the page that already covers it (deprecate the copy, add a supersedes edge), shorten (rewrite to the point, cut history), or deprecate (no longer valid, no reader, no owner).
2. Before deprecating, check whether an open bet, task, flow or agent links to it. If so, keep it and set a review date.
3. Recurring series such as weekly data packs: keep only the newest, deprecate the older ones.
4. Look for contradictions and out-of-date facts on pages you touch (targets, dates, prices, names). Fix them or mark the older page superseded.
5. Never deprecate a page named in the Wiki Coverage Bar, Wiki Home, Wiki Status, or anything a person wrote or marked as their own. Deprecation is reversible.
6. Intake rule: a new page needs an owner, a reader and a review date. Add what is missing on pages you touch, and deprecate drafts nobody will claim.

Post ONE comment on the flow, attention 2, under 80 words: pages kept, merged, shortened, deprecated, and the new Idle drafts and Stale pages numbers. Recount both with query_data (type knowledge, status draft, updated_before now-14d; and type knowledge, status validated, updated_before now-60d) and update the target numbers on the flow, keeping the labels exactly Idle drafts and Stale pages. If the flow does not have those two targets yet, add them with a target of 0. Stay silent on pages you only kept. Late start: if this runs more than 24 hours after its time, still run it.
